1. Nature. 2002 Sep 19;419(6904):269-70. doi: 10.1038/419269a.

Stimulating illusory own-body perceptions.

Blanke O(1), Ortigue S, Landis T, Seeck M.

Author information:
(1)Laboratory of Presurgical Epilepsy Evaluation, Program of Functional 
Neurology and Neurosurgery, University Hospital of Geneva, Geneva 1211, 
Switzerland. olaf.blanke@hcuge.ch

'Out-of-body' experiences (OBEs) are curious, usually brief sensations in which 
a person's consciousness seems to become detached from the body and take up a 
remote viewing position. Here we describe the repeated induction of this 
experience by focal electrical stimulation of the brain's right angular gyrus in 
a patient who was undergoing evaluation for epilepsy treatment. Stimulation at 
this site also elicited illusory transformations of the patient's arm and legs 
(complex somatosensory responses) and whole-body displacements (vestibular 
responses), indicating that out-of-body experiences may reflect a failure by the 
brain to integrate complex somatosensory and vestibular information.
